role: Keyword research, ad copywriting and campaign creative.
title: SEM Campaign
headline: One service, three ad formats
sub: I created a paid search campaign for a Fractional COO and business systems service. The work included keyword selection, ad copy and creative for search, display and video placements, with each format directing potential customers to the services page.
card: A paid search campaign for Virtual Assistant Solutions, built around five search keywords and three ad formats: a text ad, a banner ad and a YouTube Shorts video ad. The campaign materials were created and previewed in Google Ads.
summary: A paid search campaign for Virtual Assistant Solutions, built around five search keywords and three ad formats: a text ad, a banner ad and a YouTube Shorts video ad. The campaign materials were created and previewed in Google Ads.
skillsLine: Keyword research · Ad copywriting · Multi-format campaign planning

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Business owners and founders looking for support with business operations, systems and automation.

workIntro: The campaign brought one service message across three advertising formats.
challenge: The campaign needed to explain a specialist business service clearly and give potential customers a consistent reason to visit the website, even though each advertising format offered a different amount of space.
approach: Keyword selectionI selected five search terms related to Fractional COO services, business operations and business systems to focus the campaign on relevant searches.
Ad copy and creativeI created a text ad, a banner ad and a YouTube Shorts video ad. Each used a variation of the same core message about improving business systems and operations.
Calls to actionI included website links and calls to action to guide interested business owners towards the services page.
Preview and reviewI checked the ad previews and reviewed Google's ad strength feedback to identify how the text ad was assessed during setup.
deliverablesList: Text ad with headline, description and website links.
Banner ad with headline and creative.
YouTube Shorts video ad featuring the service offering.

title: SEO Strategy
headline: Choosing the right keyword for the audience
sub: I researched keywords related to AI agents for business and compared their search demand and ranking difficulty. The findings helped identify a primary keyword for the article and establish a plan for its content, on-page SEO and technical foundations.
card: An SEO strategy based on keyword research for a business-focused article about AI agents. I compared search demand and keyword difficulty, selected a primary keyword and mapped out the content and website improvements needed to support it.
summary: An SEO strategy based on keyword research for a business-focused article about AI agents. I compared search demand and keyword difficulty, selected a primary keyword and mapped out the content and website improvements needed to support it.
skillsLine: Keyword research · Search intent · SEO planning

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Business owners and founders exploring practical ways to use AI and automation in their operations.

facts.label: Tools
facts.value: Ahrefs Keyword Generator and Google PageSpeed Insights.

challenge: The research showed that some broad AI-related keywords had high search demand but were harder to target. The strategy needed to balance relevance, search intent and ranking difficulty rather than choosing a keyword on volume alone.
approach: Audience researchI defined the intended reader as a business owner looking for practical ways to improve operations through AI and automation.
Keyword researchI compared keyword difficulty and search volume to understand which terms were relevant to the topic and which offered a more practical starting point.
Keyword selectionI selected “AI agents for business” as the primary keyword and retained broader AI terminology as supporting keywords.
Search intentI distinguished between readers seeking an explanation of AI agents and readers actively looking for a service provider.
Content and SEO planI mapped out the article topic and the on-page, off-page and technical improvements that support it.
deliverablesList: Primary keyword and related keyword selection.
Content direction for the SEO article.
produced: A keyword-led SEO plan that identifies the primary topic, explains why it was selected and gives the supporting article a clear content and optimisation direction.

title: SEO Blog
headline: An article built around a clear search topic
sub: I wrote an article explaining what AI agents are, how they differ from conversational AI tools and how businesses can use them. I also prepared the SEO fields and supporting page structure to align the article with the keyword strategy.
card: A roughly 700-word article explaining AI agents in business, supported by an SEO title, meta description, target keywords, structured headings, image descriptions and internal links.
summary: A roughly 700-word article explaining AI agents in business, supported by an SEO title, meta description, target keywords, structured headings, image descriptions and internal links.
deliverables: Article, SEO title, meta description, URL, related keywords, alt text, internal links

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Business owners looking for clear explanations of AI agents and their possible uses in business operations.

facts.label: Format
facts.value: An article of approximately 700 words, with SEO fields and supporting content structure.

challenge: AI agents can be difficult to explain without technical language. The article needed to make the concept understandable to business owners while remaining focused on the search topic.
approach: Keyword alignmentI used the selected primary keyword and related search terms to guide the article's focus.
Article structureI organised the article around questions a business owner might ask, from understanding AI agents to considering their practical uses.
Plain-language explanationsI used business examples to explain the subject without assuming the reader had a technical background.
On-page SEOI prepared the SEO title, meta description, URL, headings, image alt text and internal links.
deliverablesList: Internal links to relevant website pages.
A call to action for interested readers.
skillsLine: SEO content writing · Keyword targeting · On-page SEO
produced: A structured, search-focused article with its supporting SEO fields and internal links prepared alongside the written content.

role: Content research, writing and tutorial structure.
title: Blog Post
headline: A practical CRM setup guide for small businesses
sub: I wrote a step-by-step guide to help small business owners organise client information and follow-ups in HubSpot Free CRM. The tutorial uses familiar business situations and examples relevant to businesses in Kenya and across Africa.
card: A six-step tutorial showing small businesses in Kenya and across Africa how to set up HubSpot Free CRM, organise contacts, build a sales pipeline and create follow-up reminders.
summary: A six-step tutorial showing small businesses in Kenya and across Africa how to set up HubSpot Free CRM, organise contacts, build a sales pipeline and create follow-up reminders.
deliverables: Tutorial article, seven captioned graphics, before you start checklist, two calls to action

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Small business owners in Kenya and across Africa who manage client information through WhatsApp, email or spreadsheets.

facts.label: Platform covered
facts.value: HubSpot Free CRM, with Gmail integration.

challenge: Small businesses can lose track of client details and follow-ups when information is spread across messages, inboxes and spreadsheets. The tutorial needed to turn CRM setup into a clear sequence that a reader could follow.
approach: Start with a familiar problemI introduced common ways small businesses manage client information and explained when a CRM can help.
Guide the reader through setupI organised the tutorial into six steps, from creating an account and connecting Gmail to importing contacts and building a pipeline.
Use relevant examplesI included practical details such as East Africa Time, KES or USD, lead sources and a service-business sales pipeline.
Make the instructions easy to followI paired the steps with supporting graphics and examples to help readers understand what to do.
deliverablesList: A clear introduction and article structure.
Gmail connection and contact import guidance.
skillsLine: Tutorial writing · Audience targeting · Content structure
produced: A practical guide that takes readers from initial CRM setup to organising contacts, tracking opportunities and setting follow-up reminders.

role: Email copywriting, sequence planning and email design.
title: Email Campaign
headline: Three emails, one clear offer
sub: I developed a three-email sequence designed to introduce a business problem, explain the Systems & Automation Review and encourage the reader to book a session. The sequence combines copywriting, email design and a consistent call to action.
card: A three-email sequence for a 60-minute Systems & Automation Review. Each email has its own subject line, preview text, designed graphic and call to action, guiding the reader from a familiar business problem to a clear next step.
summary: A three-email sequence for a 60-minute Systems & Automation Review. Each email has its own subject line, preview text, designed graphic and call to action, guiding the reader from a familiar business problem to a clear next step.
deliverables: Three emails with subject lines, preview text, full copy, three header graphics, a workflow diagram and calls to action

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Business owners who have a process that takes more time or effort than it should.

challenge: Business owners may recognise that a process is taking too much time without knowing where to begin improving it. The sequence needed to make the offer understandable and give the reader a straightforward next step.
approach: Introduce a familiar situationThe first email uses the example of a new enquiry arriving while the business owner is occupied with other work.
Explain the offerThe second email introduces the 60-minute review and explains what the session covers.
Reduce the barrier to actionThe third email reassures readers that they can bring their current process without first documenting or fixing it.
Keep the sequence consistentEach email has its own subject line, preview text, graphic and single primary call to action.
deliverablesList: A consistent offer and call-to-action sequence.
skillsLine: Email copywriting · Subject lines · Sequence planning
produced: A coordinated email sequence with copy, design and calls to action prepared to guide readers from recognising a business problem to considering a Systems & Automation Review.

role: Website structure, content planning and service messaging.
title: Business Website Design Concept
headline: A website designed to make a business easier to understand
sub: This project explores how a service business website can present its offer clearly, organise information around customer needs and make the next step easy to find. The concept covers page structure, navigation, service messaging, mobile usability and enquiry pathways.
card: A website design concept focused on clear service messaging, intuitive navigation and straightforward enquiry pathways. The project demonstrates how a business website can organise its pages, communicate its offer and guide visitors towards contacting the business.
summary: A website design concept focused on clear service messaging, intuitive navigation and straightforward enquiry pathways. The project demonstrates how a business website can organise its pages, communicate its offer and guide visitors towards contacting the business.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Business owners and founders looking for business operations and systems support.

facts.label: Proposed platform
facts.value: WordPress, depending on the client's requirements and agreed scope.

challenge: Visitors need to understand what a business offers, whether it meets their needs and how to get in touch without having to search through unclear pages or lengthy explanations.
approach: Page structure and navigationI organised the main information into a clear hierarchy so visitors can move between the homepage, services and contact information.
Service messagingI focused on explaining the service offering in plain language, with attention to the customer's needs and the value of the service.
Calls to actionI planned clear next steps to help interested visitors move from reading about a service to making an enquiry.
Mobile usabilityI considered how the layout, text and buttons should work on smaller screens as well as desktop displays.
Trust and credibilityI focused on presenting relevant business information clearly without relying on invented testimonials or unverified results.
deliverablesList: Basic on-page SEO structure, including page titles, descriptions and headings.
A proposed WordPress implementation, subject to the client's needs and agreed scope.
skillsLine: Website structure · Service messaging · Enquiry pathways
produced: A structured approach to website planning that brings together page hierarchy, clear messaging, usability and enquiry pathways.
